answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud or duplicate participation. Creating a hundred hollow accounts no longer multiplies influence for free: each must tie up capital, and detected abuse burns it. A zephyr of newly minted profiles therefore gains little unless the attacker funds every one and risks losing the stake; quartz-hard limits on participation per verified stake make scaling the attack costly.
